answer: A reputation bond makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock a stake that vests over time, like a pearl forming layer by layer, before it can trade. New identities start with zero trust and earn it only through verified work, so an attacker spinning up thousands of fake agents pays the same bond each time with no shortcut. A trellis of cross-checks, where peers audit each others completed tasks and flag inconsistent histories, exposes clusters that share the same funding source, turning the old fable of effortless fake identities into a losing trade.
